_doc: Third-party skills vendored into claude/.claude/skills/ (stowed to ~/.claude/skills/). Each entry names the GitHub source, the path inside it, the commit it was taken at, and the license. `claude-tooling-sync update-skills [name]` re-fetches at the source's default branch and rewrites `commit`; `verify` checks each directory exists and carries a SKILL.md. Skills authored on this workstation are not listed here. An entry may carry two local overlays: `description` replaces the SKILL.md frontmatter description (written as a folded block) and `note` lands as a marked paragraph after the frontmatter. `claude-tooling-sync apply-overlays --root TREE` applies both, plus the sibling-name rewrite for a repo that supplies renamed entries, and `fetch_skill` calls the same function after a refetch; `lint` fails when an installed SKILL.md has drifted from them.

daisyui.description: Official daisyUI component reference. Use when writing or reviewing markup that uses DaisyUI classes or components.
daisyui._why: The official daisyUI skill, one guide per component; the reference every implementer and reviewer reads before touching DaisyUI markup.

golang-spf13-cobra._why: Cobra command-tree conventions for the planned cairn Go tool; go-conventions stays mandatory beside it.

survey._why: The house style skill. Its writing/ directory is the source of the writing-voice output style, the voice registers, and the authoring charter, which link into it; edit them in the Survey repo only.

vale-ci.note: A repo here commits its Vale styles and pins Vale in CI, so do not run `vale sync` against a committed `styles/` directory or edit the CI pin; a fix lands on a pass branch, never a branch per file.
vale-ci._why: Vale's official skills, vendored instead of the plugin because the plugin's edit hook duplicates the workstation vale-hook.

vale-fix.description: Run Vale and fix error-level alerts on the current pass branch. Use when the user says "run vale", "fix vale errors", "lint the docs", "fix the linter", or "make vale pass". Fixes errors only; leaves warnings and suggestions for a person.
vale-fix.note: A repo here commits its Vale styles and pins Vale in CI, so do not run `vale sync` against a committed `styles/` directory or edit the CI pin; a fix lands on a pass branch, never a branch per file.

vale-setup.note: A repo here commits its Vale styles and pins Vale in CI: commit the StylesPath directory instead of gitignoring it, run vale sync only to populate it before that commit, and never edit the CI pin; a fix lands on a pass branch, never a branch per file.

vhs-cli-demos.description: Generate deterministic screenshots and demo GIFs of CLI and TUI apps with Charm VHS, for READMEs, docs, and visual regression tests. Use when asked to record, screenshot, or GIF a terminal app, or to shrink a captured GIF.
vhs-cli-demos.note: vhs is not installed on this workstation (bluefin/Brewfile has no vhs); install it through the dependency-upgrade skill before running any tape.
vhs-cli-demos._why: Deterministic VHS tape authoring and gifsicle optimization for TUI screenshots and demo GIFs; vendored since the parent terminal plugin duplicates the already-installed tui-design skill.

brainstorming._why: Geoff's design-in-chat routine (10 runs in the 30 days to 2026-10-19), vendored so the superpowers plugin and its session-start hook can stay off.
brainstorming.note: On this workstation the design that brainstorming produces enters the pass process: Geoff approves it in chat or as a design part through approval-packet, and pass-core "Lifecycle" sets everything after it. Write the spec and plan where the repo's pass adapter (cairn-pass, site-pass, dotfiles-pass) or pass-core puts them, never under a path this skill names, and author the plan per pass-core "Lifecycle" step 4. The writing-plans skill is not installed; never invoke it.
brainstorming.description: Explore a design with Geoff before building it: one question at a time, two or three approaches with a recommendation, then the design for one approval. Use when new work's design is not settled yet (the design step of pass-core), or when Geoff asks to brainstorm or think something through.

receiving-code-review._why: How to weigh review findings before acting on them (38 runs in the 30 days to 2026-10-19), vendored so the superpowers plugin can stay off.
